item.text: I’m checking a small set of primary and near-primary 2024 sources to separate actual course-correction from just rhetoric, then I’ll synthesize claim-level evidence for 8B.8 with both positive and negative sides.

item.text:
**Verdict**
Partly yes, but mostly in narrow economic/administrative areas. Sharif did sometimes change instruments, punish failed implementers, and rework delivery systems in 2024. But the pattern was reactive and centralized, not a broad, durable feedback loop. On media, protest, and courts, he more often doubled down on coercive control than corrected course.

**Positive evidence**
- **PM orders action over “ineffective” track, trace system** | **Dawn** | **2024-05-08** | https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117 | Claim: after an inquiry report found the FBR’s track-and-trace system ineffective, Sharif ordered action against responsible officials, which is direct course correction after a tactic failed. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.2, 8B.6
- **PM Shehbaz directs full digitalization of social welfare payments under BISP** | **APP** | **2024-03-18** | https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/ | Claim: Sharif shifted BISP disbursements to digital wallets to cut leakage, delay, and discretion, showing a method change rather than sticking with a leaky delivery system. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.3, 8B.6
- **Pakistan PM unveils broader plan to sell most state-owned firms** | **ThePrint / Reuters** | **2024-05-14** | https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-unveils-broader-plan-to-sell-most-state-owned-firms/2084587/ | Claim: Sharif expanded privatization to most SOEs after fiscal strain, a reallocation away from state rents toward a different economic implementation model. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.2, 8B.6
- **Shehbaz Sharif directs to minimize load-shedding** | **Radio Pakistan** | **2024-05-28** | https://www.radio.gov.pk/28-05-2024/shehbaz-sharif-directs-to-minimize-load-shedding | Claim: he ordered a tighter anti-power-theft campaign with monthly reviews, task forces, and provincial and law-enforcement support, showing operational adaptation and closer control. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.6
- **Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says** | **Reuters / Investing.com** | **2024-09-07** | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/pakistan-renegotiating-power-deals-to-cut-costs-minister-says-3606192 | Claim: the government renegotiated expensive power contracts because households and firms were under pressure, which is a concrete response to a failing cost structure. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.2, 8B.6
- **IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation for Pakistan** | **IMF** | **2024-09-27** | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr | Claim: the IMF said growth returned, inflation fell to single digits, and reserves doubled over the prior year, so some policy adjustments were working. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.7, 8B.2
- **Pakistan to investigate army’s meddling in judiciary, law minister says** | **Reuters via Al Jazeera** | **2024-03-28** | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says | Claim: after judges alleged ISI intimidation, the government said it would form an inquiry commission, which is limited but real willingness to surface a politically sensitive abuse claim. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6

**Negative evidence**
- **Pakistan’s new government should protect rights** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-03-11** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/11/pakistan-new-government-should-protect-rights | Claim: HRW said Sharif inherited a deep rights crisis and that the government had not yet reversed the clampdown on dissent, which weighs against a strong “correct course” reading. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6
- **Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-01-11** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent | Claim: HRW described pressure on media, opposition, and NGOs, plus weak safeguards for vulnerable people, showing continuity of coercive methods rather than correction. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6
- **The state acknowledged blocking X on national-security grounds** | **Reuters / Investing.com** | **2024-04-17** | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313 | Claim: the government confirmed blocking X during a politically sensitive period, which is evidence of information control rather than adaptive openness. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6
- **Pakistan: the new peaceful assembly and public order act threatens the right to protest** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-09-09** | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/ | Claim: instead of loosening coercive tactics after earlier backlash, the government tightened protest restrictions through law. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6
- **Pakistan government intensifies crackdown political dissent** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-10-09** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent | Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts, indicating the state responded to dissent by escalating repression. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6
- **Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs** | **The Guardian** | **2024-10-21** | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps | Claim: critics said the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence amid intimidation allegations, cutting against institutional self-correction and neutral oversight. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6
- **Pakistan: Respect Rights in Response to Balochistan March** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-07-31** | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/pakistan-respect-rights-response-balochistan-march | Claim: authorities detained hundreds and cut internet access during the Baloch march, showing a tendency to meet failed control with more control. | **IDs:** 8B.8, 8B.5, 8B.6

**Search gap**
I found solid evidence of tactical adaptation in economic management and a few discrete investigations, but not strong evidence of a sustained, system-wide habit of replacing ineffective implementers or institutionalizing feedback. Most positive items are reactive, sector-specific, or top-down. The strongest counterpattern is that when political control was challenged, Sharif’s government often tightened restrictions instead of changing course.
